lines.text: December, nineteen hundred. Three lighthouse keepers vanish from a Scottish island. The story you've heard? Fake.
Eleven days later, a relief ship arrives. Nobody's waiting on the dock.
The door is shut. The beds are unmade. Two raincoats are gone. One still hangs on its peg.
No half eaten dinner. No overturned chair. Those come from a poem, written twelve years later.
The famous logbook entries, the praying, the crying? First confirmed in print in nineteen sixty five. Fiction.
But the rocks don't lie. A boulder over a ton, shoved out of place. Damage a hundred feet up the cliff.
Best guess? A freak wave swept all three off the landing.
The legend is fiction. The men are still gone.
